findings.title: Missing URL encoding of customerId in API client enables path traversal against MonetizeKit API server
findings.description: The `MonetizeKitClient` methods `getEntitlement()`, `getUsage()`, and `getCredits()` interpolate the `customerId` parameter directly into URL paths without `encodeURIComponent()`. Meanwhile, the adjacent `featureKey` and `meterId` parameters in the same methods ARE properly encoded. This inconsistency allows path traversal characters (e.g., `../`) or URL metacharacters (`?`, `#`) in `customerId` to alter the request target, sending authenticated requests to unintended endpoints on the MonetizeKit API origin.
findings.impact: If a consuming application derives `customerId` from user-influenced input (URL parameters, form fields, decoded JWT claims), an attacker can craft a `customerId` containing path traversal sequences (e.g., `../../admin/users`) that cause the SDK to send authenticated GET requests (carrying the publishable key as a Bearer token and the optional customer JWT in X-Customer-Token) to arbitrary paths on the MonetizeKit API server. This could expose sensitive data or trigger unintended server-side actions depending on what endpoints exist at the traversed paths.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker influences the `customerId` value in a consuming application (e.g., via URL query parameter `?customer=../../admin` or manipulated session data).
2. The consuming app passes the attacker-controlled value as `customerId` to `<MonetizeKitProvider customerId={userInput}>`.
3. SDK hooks (`useEntitlement`, `useUsage`, `useCredits`) forward the unencoded `customerId` to `MonetizeKitClient` methods.
4. The client constructs URLs like `GET {baseUrl}/api/v1/entitlements/../../admin/users/{encodedFeatureKey}`.
5. The browser resolves the path traversal, sending the request to e.g. `GET {baseUrl}/admin/users/{encodedFeatureKey}` with valid Authorization and X-Customer-Token headers.
findings.poc_video_notes: A PoC video is not feasible because the vulnerability is in URL construction within the client-side SDK. Demonstrating it requires a running MonetizeKit API backend that is not available in this environment. The issue can be verified by code inspection: the inconsistent encoding of customerId vs featureKey/meterId in the same method signatures is clear evidence of the bug.
